gloss: to think of, to hit upon

definitions.gloss: to think of, to come up with
definitions.explanation: To have an idea suddenly come to mind.

examples.japanese: ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: I thought of a good idea.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何|なに}か→何：00498_nani⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いたら⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧。
examples.english: Let me know if you think of something.

examples.japanese: ⟦{急|きゅう}に→急：13042_kyuu⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いた。
⟦{解決策|かいけつさく}→解決策：19395_kaiketsusaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: I came up with a solution.

examples.japanese: ⟦シャワー→シャワー：04503_shawaa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浴|あ}びている→浴びる：02844_abiru⟧⟦とき→時：02918_toki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦アイデア→アイデア：10161_aidea⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}くこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: I often come up with new ideas while taking a shower.

notes:
{思|おも}い{付|つ}く is a godan verb meaning to think of or come up with an idea, often suddenly.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive)
- The idea is the subject: ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いた
- Can also use を: ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いた

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}く: to think of a good idea
- ⟦{急|きゅう}に→急：13042_kyuu⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}く: to suddenly occur to one
- ⟦{何|なに}か→何か：03873_nanika⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いたら: if you think of something

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{思|おも}い{付|つ}き→思い付き：27771_omoitsuki⟧: a (sudden) idea, whim
- ⟦{思|おも}い{付|つ}き→思い付き：27771_omoitsuki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧: on a whim

SIMILAR VERBS:
- ⟦{思|おも}い{出|だ}す→思い出す：01258_omoidasu⟧: to remember, recall
- ⟦{気|き}が{付|つ}く→気がつく：21794_kigatsuku⟧: to notice, realize
- ⟦{考|かんが}え{付|つ}く→考え付く：27772_kangaetsuku⟧: to think up, devise

ASPECT (ている):
- {思|おも}い{付|つ}いている: has thought of / has an idea in mind (resultative state)
- Note: {思|おも}い{付|つ}く is a punctual verb — the idea arrives in an instant. The ている form describes the resulting state of already having the idea, not the process of thinking. ⟦{何|なに}か→何か：03873_nanika⟧{思|おも}い{付|つ}いている？ is more naturally "Do you have any ideas?" than "Are you in the middle of thinking one up?"
